RSS headline: "One killed, 11 injured in second Houthi strike on Riyadh airport in two days"
JSON-LD headline: "Saudi Arabia's Riyadh airport hit by second Houthi strike in two days"

ONE killed and ELEVEN injured in a strike on King Khalid International Airport, Riyadh, on Sunday.
A Saudi military spokesman said a projectile hit the airport, causing a fire in one of its passenger halls.
Saudi Arabia's civil aviation authority said on X that the person killed was a PAKISTANI RESIDENT.
Comes a day after a strike on the same airport KILLED 13 and INJURED 308, following similar strikes earlier in the week.

The Houthis in Yemen said they were behind the attacks and warned airlines and passengers against using Saudi airports and airspace.
The group said it targeted the airport with a mix of ballistic and cruise missiles plus drones in the past 24 hours. They also attacked oil facilities and DAMMAM airport in eastern Saudi Arabia, their military spokesman BRIG GEN YAHYA SAREE said.
Saree vowed to continue "escalating operations deep inside Saudi Arabia", warning that ALL Saudi airports were potential targets APART FROM those in Mecca and Medina.
The Houthis say they are targeting Saudi Arabia over its support for government forces in Yemen's civil war, and over an air strike on Sanaa airport.
MAJ GEN TURKI AL-MALIKI, spokesman for the Saudi-led coalition, said Sunday that air defences intercepted a missile near the Riyadh airport, while authorities dealt with a fire caused by an "unknown projectile" that hit PASSENGER HALL NO 4.

RESPONSES: Trump said the US would "make a decision" and "move very quickly" on whether to strike the Houthis.
UK Defence Secretary WES STREETING suggested the UK could "potentially" provide more support for Saudi Arabia.
US Secretary of State MARCO RUBIO condemned the attacks and confirmed a US citizen was killed.
Foreign Secretary ED MILIBAND said he was "appalled".
The UK Foreign Office is advising against all travel to parts of Saudi Arabia, including within 10km (6.2 miles) of the Yemen border; other western embassies have warned nationals about travel in the region.

SATURDAY TOLL DETAIL: deadliest single attack on a Gulf Arab country since the war between Israel, the US and Iran began in February. Saudi-led coalition vowed to respond, calling it a "war crime".
Dead included four Saudi nationals, two people from Bangladesh and one person each from the US, Jordan, Palestine, Syria, Sudan and Egypt (Saudi civil aviation authority). The Indian embassy said on Sunday an Indian man had succumbed to his injuries.

UNVERIFIED: Houthi-run Al Masirah TV said "the Saudi enemy" launched an air strike on Sanaa International Airport; a residential home in the city was also struck, killing a child and injuring six. "Saudi Arabia has not confirmed the attacks and the BBC has been unable to verify this."
